class.name: PhysXWaterWake3D
class.brief_description: The wake and foam a [RigidBody3D] leaves on a [PhysXWaterSurface3D] as it moves.
class.description: Add as a child of a [RigidBody3D] -- a boat, usually alongside a [PhysXBuoyancy3D] and a [PhysXBoat3D]. It runs a small ripple simulation on the GPU, centered a little behind the body, that the hull pushes down as it moves: a row of dips along its keel, deeper with speed. The grid is fixed to the water, not the body: as it slides along with the body, the waves and foam stay where they were made and fade out behind, and waves reaching the grid's edge are absorbed rather than reflected back. A boat at speed draws a Kelvin wake. The wake is drawn by the water surface's material and included in [method PhysXWaterSurface3D.sample_height], so other floating bodies ride it -- everywhere there is water, past the surface's simulated square and over its shore ripple grid alike. The body's own [PhysXBuoyancy3D] doesn't float on its own wake. A surface draws up to four wakes. It also carries foam, in two layers: - [b]Hull foam[/b]: churned into a band just outside the hull along its sides, heaviest at the bow ([member bow_foam]), then pushed out sideways from the hull's line ([member foam_spread]) so it peels off into the two bands of a boat's wake. Steep wake waves break into it too ([member foam_slope]). Foam added with [method add_foam] drifts out with it. - [b]Propeller foam[/b]: churned in behind a sibling [PhysXBoat3D]'s propeller with its thrust ([member propeller_foam]); it stays where it was made, a band down the middle. Both fade over [member foam_persistence]. The grid has to cover the wake to keep it: a body turning tight circles needs a [member size] that holds the circle for its wake to close into a ring, and a [member foam_persistence] of about one lap. Water with an interactive shore ripple grid can carry a body's ripples there instead (see [member PhysXBuoyancy3D.disturb_water]); [member shore_grid_fade] fades the wake out over that grid.

method.name: add_foam
method.description: Churns foam into the wake's water around [param world_position] on the next physics step: [param amount_per_second] at the center (1 is fully white), fading out over [param radius] meters. Call it every tick for a steady source, or once with an amount divided by the physics delta for a one-off patch. With [param drift], the foam is pushed out from the hull's line with the hull foam, heading out into the wake; without, it stays where it was put. [PhysXWaterSpray3D] uses this for the foam its spray leaves.

method.name: get_grid_origin
method.description: The world XZ of the grid's corner, as last stepped. The grid spans [member size] meters from there along +X and +Z.

method.name: get_height_texture
method.description: The wake's texture, as the water material draws it: red the height (m), green the hull foam, blue the propeller foam (0 to 1).

method.name: sample_height
method.description: The wake's height (m) at [param world_pos]'s XZ, from the last readback (a few frames behind the simulation); [code]0[/code] outside the grid. The water surface adds it into its own [method PhysXWaterSurface3D.sample_height].

members.member: Damping per second at the grid's edge, easing in across the outer tenth of it: waves running into the border are absorbed instead of reflecting back at the body.
Hull foam churned in per second at the bow, along the hull's sides, at [member reference_speed]; it tapers off toward the stern and scales with speed.

Grid cells per side. With [member size] this sets the cell size: keep it around 0.25 m for crisp foam and short wake waves. The cost grows with the square of it; the GPU step is cheap, but the readback for [method sample_height] grows the same way.
How quickly the wake's waves die out, per second.
Seconds the foam takes to fade to about a third.
The wake wave slope past which waves break into hull foam.
Foam per second per unit of slope past [member foam_slope].
How fast (m/s) the hull foam is pushed out sideways from the hull's line at full speed -- strongest near the hull, fading out over about three beams -- so it opens into two bands behind the boat.
The hull's width (m). [code]0[/code] takes it from the sibling [PhysXBuoyancy3D]'s sample points.
The hull's length (m) along its [code]+Z[/code]. [code]0[/code] takes it from the sibling [PhysXBuoyancy3D]'s sample points.
Propeller foam churned in per second at full thrust, behind a sibling [PhysXBoat3D]'s propeller. [code]0[/code] turns it off.
The speed (m/s) at which the hull dips to [member wake_depth] and churns [member bow_foam]; faster goes up to 1.5 times that.
How far (m) the hull pushes the water down at rest.

How much the wake fades out over the water surface's simulated shore square: [code]0[/code] draws it everywhere (open water, an ocean), [code]1[/code] leaves that square to the body's [PhysXBuoyancy3D] ripples (a lake, where the interactive ripples are worth their cost). In between blends the two.

The grid's side length (m). Going straight, most of it trails behind the body; it has to cover all of a wake to keep it, so a body turning tight circles needs one that holds the circle. Changing it rebuilds the grid.
How many dips the hull is pushed down as, spread along its keel from bow to stern.
How far (m) the hull pushes the water down at the bow at [member reference_speed]; shallower toward the stern.
The [PhysXWaterSurface3D] to draw on. Empty uses the sibling [PhysXBuoyancy3D]'s.
How fast (m/s) the wake's waves travel. With the body's speed it sets the wake's angle: slower waves give a narrower V.
